svg.title: How a run works
svg.desc: How a run works, with the counts of SetuHQ's stored run on pi Men (TESS sector 1): 1. Ingest (TESS, CHEOPS, CSV): 1 light curve of 3,485 points; 2. Clean (clip, detrend, bin): masked local-quadratic baseline, 10-minute bins; 3. Blind-code (13-day subjects): 2 subjects, no target names; 4. Review (the panel marks dips): 2 Sentinels + 3 Probes; 10 classifications; 5. Aggregate (skill-weighted consensus): 7 consensus dips; 6. Vet (SNR, odd/even, secondary): 6 passed (1 flagged off-ephemeris), 1 rejected; 7. Fit (limb-darkened transit): 5 of 5 epochs on the ephemeris; Rp/R★ 0.0179; 8. FAP (block bootstrap): < 10⁻⁴ over 10,000 trials: a bound, not a value; 9. Write (candidates + provenance): CSV, JSON, SQLite, a manifest and the site. Every step's output is kept, so a run can be re-vetted from its stored classifications without asking the reviewers again. Sources: runs/tess-pi-men-s1 (manifest.json, candidates.json, subjects), configs/tess_pi_men_s1.toml and docs/results/pi_men_validation.json, commit b742c73.
